newsitem.title: USA: U.S. IPOs drop sharply in April - study.
newsitem.headline: U.S. IPOs drop sharply in April - study.

text.p: The number of initial public offerings dropped off sharply to 28 in April, the lowest in more than two years, according to Securities Data Co.
It was the lowest number of new equity issues since January 1995, when only 18 deals went public, excluding closed end funds and real estate investment trusts.
April IPOs raised $1.29 billion, not a record low for this year, but only the fourth month in the past two years in which monthly proceeds were under $2 billion.
Three large IPOs accounted for 60 percent of the money raised.

Hertz Corp raised $438 million, Long Beach Financial Corp $141 million and Cornerstone Properties Inc raised $196 million. Without those large offerings, April IPOs would have raised less than $520 million, the lowest since February 1991, Securities Data said.

Many investment firms, including Salomon Brothers, Morgan Stanley & Co and Hambrecht & Quist did not take any new companies public in April. High technology issues raised only $223 million, or 17 percent of the month's volume.
Securities Data Co, based in Newark, N.J., provides financing and merger data.
